description: Conformance fixture for serializePayload (packages/schema/src/shrink.ts), regenerated by gen-shrink.mjs. For each case: expand the input, call serializePayload(input, maxBytes ?? MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, type) (no "type" = called without one), and compare the JSON text byte for byte and the truncated flag. Version-1 cases keep their names and inputs ("since": 1); "v1" says whether the expected output changed from version 1 and why.
generator: Expand recursively before calling serializePayload. An object whose ONLY key is one of these stands for: "$repeat": [unit, count] -> unit repeated count times; "$array": [item, count] -> an array of count expanded copies of item; "$concat": [part, ...] -> the expanded string parts joined; "$keys": [prefix, count, item] -> an object with keys prefix+"0" .. prefix+(count-1), in that order, each an expanded copy of item (prefix "" gives integer-like keys, ascending: the JSON of a typed array); "$merge": [object, ...] -> the expanded objects shallow-merged in order (no case repeats a key). Object key order is as written; "__proto__" is an ordinary own key. Expected results of up to 16 KB carry the exact "json" text; larger ones carry "jsonBytes" (UTF-8 length), "jsonSha256" (hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 json text) and the first/last 160 UTF-16 units for diagnostics. No object mixes integer-like keys with other keys (JavaScript would enumerate the integer-like ones first).
skeleton: "skeletonPlans" lists, per known event type, its schema keys in declaration order: null = a required field (kept, hard-shrunk); a nested object = a required loose-object field (kept as an object of its own planned keys, recursively); "optional" = an optional field, kept (hard-shrunk) only when its value is a string, number or boolean. Types not listed get no skeleton (whole-payload marker). Skeleton attempts, first that validates and fits wins: [SKELETON_CHARS, preview + fields], [SKELETON_CHARS, preview "" and no fields], [SKELETON_MIN_CHARS, preview "" and no fields]. See the TIERS comment in shrink.ts.

cases.name: under-budget-object
cases.note: An ordinary node.finished payload is returned untouched (truncated false, json is plain JSON.stringify).

cases.name: under-budget-exactly-at-limit
cases.note: JSON text of exactly MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES UTF-8 bytes is within budget (the check is bytes > maxBytes).

cases.name: one-byte-over-limit
cases.note: One byte over: the field is shrunk and the marker merged in.

cases.name: multibyte-under-by-units-over-by-bytes
cases.note: The budget check is UTF-8 BYTES: "é" x 262,141 is 262,149 UTF-16 units of JSON (under 512 KB) but 524,290 bytes (2 over).

cases.name: huge-ascii-string-field
cases.note: node.finished with a 600 KB ASCII string output: output becomes a 2,000-unit prefix + suffix; structural fields kept; fields ["output"].

cases.name: huge-cjk-string-field-mixed-units
cases.note: Field sizes are UTF-16 LENGTHS subtracted from a UTF-8 BYTE total: "中" x 200,000 is ~600 KB of bytes but only ~200 KB of units, so `remaining` stays above maxBytes/2 and EVERY field (even the small ones, unchanged) is listed in `fields`.

cases.name: run-started-huge-meta-small-budget

cases.name: huge-loose-field-before-required
cases.note: A 700 KB loose field inserted before the required fields: the field trim cuts it and keeps everything else.

cases.name: huge-loose-field-before-required-small-budget
cases.note: The same shape at maxBytes 4096: the trim does not fit (2,000-unit field + 2,000-unit preview); the skeleton keeps nodeId, kind, name, instanceId and lists blob and input.

cases.name: astral-at-256-cut-skeleton-no-preview
cases.note: maxBytes 4096, message = 255 "a" then emoji: the skeleton cuts it at 256 units, splitting a surrogate pair (JSON writes the lone high half as \ud83d). With the 2,000-unit preview the first attempt is over budget, so the second attempt (preview "", no fields) is used.

cases.name: cjk-at-256-cut-skeleton-multibyte-preview
cases.note: maxBytes 8192, a message of 5,000 "中": the trim does not fit (2,000 CJK units in the field and in the preview); the first skeleton attempt does — 256 CJK units plus a 2,000-unit preview.

cases.name: astral-at-2000-cut-field-trim
cases.note: The field trim cuts the output at 2,000 units, between the halves of a surrogate pair.

cases.name: escape-heavy-skeleton-min-chars
cases.note: maxBytes 4096, three required strings of 300 U+0001 (6 bytes of JSON each): 256-unit strings cannot fit even without the preview, so the third attempt cuts them at SKELETON_MIN_CHARS (32) units.

cases.name: unknown-type-whole-marker
cases.note: A type the schema does not know gets no skeleton: 300 fields fall back to the whole-payload marker, exactly as without a type.

cases.name: invalid-input-with-type-whole-marker
cases.note: A node.finished without its required status is not a valid event to begin with: the skeleton cannot validate, so the whole-payload marker is returned.

cases.name: nested-key-cap-and-exact-256
cases.note: Inside a shrunk field, an object of 300 keys (depth 1) keeps 256 and gets __graphmindTruncated + keysDropped 44 (no bytes/preview below the top); an object of exactly 256 keys is not capped.

cases.name: top-level-field-cap
cases.note: A capped object AT the top of a field: its kept keys, then __graphmindTruncated, bytes (JSON length in UTF-16 units) and preview, then keysDropped.

cases.name: proto-key-is-an-ordinary-key
cases.note: A payload key named "__proto__" is an ordinary own key (as JSON.parse, Python and Ruby treat it) and is shrunk like any other.

cases.name: graph-hint-skeleton-empty-array
cases.note: The skeleton keeps a required array as [] (verbatim only if it was already empty, so `nodes` is listed).

cases.name: exec-paused-skeleton-drops-optional-object
cases.note: maxBytes 4096: the skeleton keeps pauseId, nodeId, point and the optional string reason; the optional OBJECT loop is dropped and listed in `fields`.

cases.name: run-finished-400-small-fields-trimmed
cases.note: run.finished with 400 small loose fields and a 700 KB error.message: 400 <= MAX_TRIM_FIELDS, so the field trim runs and keeps every small field; only error is shrunk (its message cut to PREVIEW_CHARS). With the old 256-field gate this went to the skeleton and lost them.

cases.name: many-small-fields-trim-keeps-them
cases.note: MAX_TRIM_FIELDS (4,096), not MAX_SHRINK_KEYS, gates the field trim: 300 small top-level fields plus one huge output are trimmed field by field, so every small field survives.

cases.name: over-max-trim-fields-goes-to-skeleton
cases.note: More than MAX_TRIM_FIELDS (4,096) top-level fields: the field trim is not attempted and the skeleton is used.

cases.name: node-token-trim-keeps-deltas-array
cases.note: An oversized delta batch: the field trim turns deltas into [] (still a valid node.token).
